Today's verdict NEUTRAL-CAUTIOUS
When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **1/10**: near-zero realized stress, spot prices calm vs VIX Spike Tier **2/4**: backwardation and skew both active, **60%** spike probability
Spot prices are not stressed; the options market is paying up for protection anyway. When skew and backwardation fire without a price breakdown, hedgers are anticipating, not reacting. The VIX detector wins this read: options markets price the next 30 days, not the last week. With two of three sub-signals lit and the adaptive component quiet, the picture is elevated tail-risk awareness without a confirmed trend break. The gap between realized calm and implied fear is the risk to respect.
Today's tension
Price action is quiet but the options market is leaning defensive, and every major equity region closed the five-day window in the red.
Bull
The Crash Index sits at **1/10** with almost no realized stress registered. The contrarian score at **52** is a partial accumulate signal, meaning the risk/reward on the long side is improving into this pullback.
Bear
The VIX Spike Detector is at Tier **2/4** with a **60%** spike probability, and both skew and backwardation are active. Of **43** tracked cross-asset pairs, **17** are moving in the bearish direction against only **3** bullish, a net bearish bias of **14**.
The tell: Watch whether VIX backwardation resolves or deepens toward Tier **3**. Resolution signals the options market is unwinding its defensive positioning; a deepening confirms stress is building beneath calm spot prices.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The setup as of today is calm surfaces hiding a defensive underbelly. The regime scores STABLE at 36 but carries a risk-off bias from 3 aligned risk-off signals. Those two readings are coherent: stable means the system has not broken down, while the risk-off lean shows directional pressure building from inside. You have a contrarian partial accumulate signal at 52 sitting alongside a VIX Spike Detector at Tier 2/4 with a 60% spike probability. One tells you the dip is buyable; the other says the options market disagrees.

Keep any long add conservative. The accumulate signal is partial, not a full conviction read, which means the contrarian case is incomplete. With 17 of 43 tracked cross-asset pairs in bearish territory against only 3 bullish, the internal cross-market pressure is running against a risk-on add. Nearly half of all pairs (46.5%) are moving in diverging directions. You do not press size into a tape where that many relationships are breaking down simultaneously.

The single reading that flips the stance is the VIX term structure. If backwardation resolves and the detector drops from Tier 2 toward Tier 1, the risk-off signals lose their anchor and the contrarian accumulate call becomes actionable with more conviction. Until that happens, the asymmetry favors defending existing exposure over aggressively building new ones.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The INFLATIONARY regime label carries a confidence of only 30%, which tells you this is a fragile, contested designation. Low confidence means the inputs are mixed: some inflationary signals are present but not dominant enough to commit to a clean regime call.

In a confirmed inflationary regime you tilt toward real assets and commodities and away from long duration. At 30% confidence, those tilts should be modest.

The regime is better described as ambiguous than inflationary, and ambiguity favors staying near neutral on regime-sensitive trades until that confidence reading rises materially.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence here means cross-asset pairs that normally move together are pulling apart, or pairs that normally move inversely are converging unexpectedly. The shift in that relationship over time is the correlation drift.

With 46.5% of 43 tracked pairs now diverging and a net bearish bias of 14 (17 bearish vs. 3 bullish), the composite sits at ELEVATED with a Mother Jaws score of 100.

Six pairs are flashing deep divergence. The VIX-MOVE pair drifted from +0.18 to +0.79, meaning equity vol (VIX) and bond vol (the MOVE index) are now moving in lockstep: fear is spreading across asset classes rather than staying contained to one corner of the market.

The KRE-XLF pair collapsed from +0.09 to -0.59, which means regional banks and broad financials are now moving against each other; something is stressing regional bank stocks specifically while the broader financial sector holds relatively better. The ETH-BTC correlation jumped from +0.06 to +0.64, meaning crypto is trading as a single risk block rather than on asset-specific fundamentals.

These cross-asset dislocations rarely self-correct quickly.

AI read · what the confluences mean now

None of the three tracked confluence conditions are active today. VIX backwardation is firing in isolation but has not combined with credit stress via HYG, small-cap drawdown, or yen safe-haven flows to produce a compounding stress signal.

That absence is informative: the stress is single-threaded. When backwardation shows up without credit or currency confirmation, the case for a sustained vol expansion is weaker.

The higher-conviction stress setup requires at least two of those three legs to engage simultaneously. For now, backwardation is a warning with incomplete corroboration.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Asia is splitting sharply: the KOSPI is the five-day leader at +3.3% while the Hang Seng is the laggard at -3.3%, a 6.6 percentage-point spread within the same region over the same period. Europe is uniformly down, with the SMI the weakest at -4.3% and the Euro Stoxx 50 the relative survivor at -1.1%.

The US is also negative, with the S&P 500 at -1.3% and the Russell 2000 at -2.8%; small-cap underperforming large-cap is consistent with the risk-off bias in the regime reading. Crypto is the outlier: ETH is up +2.0% on the week while BTC is flat at +0.0%.

ETH outperforming BTC in a weak equity environment connects directly to the ETH-BTC correlation drift flagged in the divergence section. The KOSPI's strength deserves attention as a potential early signal for Asian risk appetite returning, but the HSI's concurrent -3.3% argues against reading it as a regional trend.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 1/10 and the VIX Spike Detector at Tier 2/4 are reading different horizons, and their divergence is coherent. The Crash Index scans current realized stress: drawdowns, dislocations, vol-of-vol.

At 1/10, all of those are quiet. The VIX Spike Detector reads the options market's forward expectation: skew is active (the market is paying a premium for downside protection over upside exposure) and backwardation is active (near-term options cost more than longer-dated ones, which means the market is pricing near-term fear above normal levels).

Both conditions are live while the adaptive component is not, which holds the reading at Tier 2 rather than pushing it higher. Price has not broken yet, but the options market is charging for insurance.

That gap between realized calm and implied fear is a structural warning, not noise.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.
Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
